uncited: Ray Marching Optimization encompasses techniques that reduce the computational cost of evaluating participating media during ray traversal, distinct from spatial acceleration structures that skip empty space.
While [Ray-grid traversal](17-ray-grid-traversal.md) determines *where* to sample, these methods optimize the *cost* of the sampling and material evaluation at those points.

They achieve this through traversal order precomputation, memory-efficient tiling, material simplification (e.g., grayscale evaluation), conservative density gating, and geometric coherence exploitation (e.g., epipolar binary trees).
All methods in this family build on [Ray-grid traversal](17-ray-grid-traversal.md), which advances analytically from one cell boundary to the next .
The core mechanism determines the next cell by comparing distances to upcoming boundaries on the x, y, and z axes, selecting the minimum distance to advance .
Optimization and cost models do not alter this fundamental geometric logic but instead optimize the *cost* of executing it or the *parameters* (like grid resolution) under which it runs.
Estimate normal $n_g$ at vertex $x_g$ based on distances $d_N, d_S, d_E, d_W$ at neighboring ray samples in concentric hemispherical mapping.
- **Definition**: An optimization that eliminates repetitive matrix transformation computations for sampling coordinates by pre-computing ray parameters.
Viewing angles and distances cannot be adjusted because pre-computation assumes rays are always fixed.
Ray marching optimization has evolved from basic traversal logic to sophisticated shader-level and data-structure-driven techniques.
